raw_response:
I have been on this land for 40 years, and the wheat-maize rotation is what I know. My 6 mu is not much, but it feeds us and we sell some. My husband and I are the only two, so I cannot waste money, but I also cannot afford a bad harvest — at our age, one bad year hurts for long.

Last year I planted Jimai 22 for wheat, it did well, gave me about 450 kg per mu. I will plant it again. For maize I use Zhengdan 958 — everyone in our village plants it, and it handles our summer heat. These hybrid seeds cost more than saving my own, but the yield is worth it.

For fertilizer, I follow what the dealer recommends and what I have done for years. For wheat, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu at sowing, that is 50 jin, and then topdress urea at jointing, about 20 jin per mu. That gives me enough nitrogen. The soil here has been farmed long, phosphorus builds up, but I still put some. For maize after wheat, I do similar — compound at sowing, urea at big trumpet stage. Maize is hungrier than wheat.

Irrigation: I have my well, so water is not a problem except for electricity cost. Wheat I water after sowing, then winter water, then at jointing, then at heading — four times. Maize usually two waterings if summer rain is normal, sometimes three if dry.

Pesticide: wheat I spray twice — once for aphids at heading, once mixed with herbicide earlier. Maize I spray once or twice for borer. I do not spray too much, it costs money.

Tillage: after maize harvest I use rotary tiller before wheat. After wheat I do no-till for maize, just drill it in — saves time and money, and the stubble helps.
